# Evidence records

Use [project status](../status.md) to see what works now. Use this catalog to
inspect the report behind a claim. Records describe what was known at the
time; their next-step suggestions may have been superseded by
[current work](../live-capture.md#current-work-order).

## Catalog

Newest record IDs appear first. IDs reflect recording order, not execution
dates: a reconstructed record may describe an older event. Provenance describes
where a report came from, not whether the test succeeded.

## Reading historical records

Each numbered record preserves the original procedure, observation, provenance
and limits. The [generated status index](../status.md) keeps every historical
heading as a compatibility link. E63–E71 were reconstructed from previously
merged documentation: missing original dates, revisions and raw reports remain
unknown. The metadata category `device_report` describes the source of a
report, including failures; it does not certify success or headset acceptance.

Long capability summaries have [supporting notes](capability-notes.md). The
[November 7 history-rewrite map](../history-rewrite-2026-11-07.txt) relates old
and new project commit IDs; upstream source pins and artifact hashes retain
their own identities.

documentation merge allocates no new evidence IDs.

## Maintaining evidence

The coordinator alone allocates evidence IDs, after checking pending allocations
in other work and open pull requests. Add the next unused ID to
`index.json` and its Markdown file; record execution date, platform/runtime,
checkout/binary revision, procedure, result and limits. Separate offline
checks, CI, user reports, upstream claims and physical recovery. Keep private
images, recordings, calibration, credentials and downloaded models out of Git.

Update reviewed capability rows in `../status-data.json` and regenerate:

```bash
python3 scripts/generate_status.py
python3 scripts/generate_status.py --check
```

The generator is dependency-free and rejects duplicate IDs, missing records,
path traversal, unknown evidence references and lost reconstructed provenance.
The capability groups in `../status-data.json` must include every capability
exactly once. Edit the three capability-row fields (`capability`, `state`,
`evidence`) there; keep detailed facts and limits in the linked evidence or
[supporting notes](capability-notes.md).

The generator owns all of `../status.md`, the marked architecture progress block
and the marked catalog above. It preserves prose outside both marked blocks.
Generated summaries must be reviewed; changing metadata never qualifies a
hardware mapping or supplies missing device evidence.
